title: Ephemeral Tenant Bridging & Priority Crediting for Dedicated Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Short PRD describing a lightweight "ephemeral tenant bridging" feature that allows short-term, controlled spillover from reserved pools into a transient buffer with a crediting mechanism (priority credits) that preserves fairness across tenants. This feature is intended to reduce hard rejections during short bursts while keeping isolation guarantees for long-running or high-priority tenants.
goals: Reduce token or request rejections for tenants experiencing short, infrequent bursts (<60s) without increasing sustained noise across pools.
Provide a transparent priority-credit accounting system that records spillover usage and influences later scheduling decisions (decay window).
Maintain per-tenant isolation SLOs: no tenant can cause >5% degraded tail latency for higher-tier tenants in the same zone over a 1h window.
Make the feature configurable per-reservation and per-tenant with sensible defaults for current Dedicated customers.
non_goals: Replace existing reserved capacity or dedicated autoscale contracts; this is a damage-mitigation layer for short bursts.
Full economic re-billing or credit settlement system (billing team will scope separate work).
Cross-region bridging of capacity or global bursting.
user_stories: As an engineering lead for a SaaS customer, I want temporary bursts handled gracefully so my app doesn't receive 429s for short traffic spikes.
As a platform operator, I want fine-grained telemetry on which tenants used ephemeral bridging so we can audit fairness and investigate regressions.
As a product manager, I want controls to tune soft-reserve window length and maximum spillover rate per pool so we can iterate on defaults.
As a high-tier tenant, I want assurance that other tenants' bursts will not push my tail latency above SLA thresholds.
functional_requirements: FR-1: Add an ephemeral buffer per dedicated pool (configurable boolean) that can accept requests when pool shortfall is detected for <= burst_window_seconds (default 60s).
FR-2: Implement a per-tenant priority credit ledger that records ephemeral buffer consumption in tokens (approx. token-equivalent units).
FR-3: Credits decay on a configurable half-life (default 24h) and affect priority weight during scheduling for next 24h to discourage repeated bursting abuse.
FR-4: Expose controls in Console and API: enable/disable ephemeral bridging for a reservation, set max spillover QPS and burst_window_seconds, and a per-tenant max_daily_ephemeral_tokens.

FR-5: When pool depletion is detected, route requests to ephemeral buffer up to pool-level cap; beyond cap return graceful 429 with structured error explaining credit exhaustion and fallback suggestions.
FR-6: Implement graceful degradation policy: prioritize requests by (tier_weight / (1 + credit_balance)) so tenants with high credit usage are deprioritized during constrained windows.
FR-7: Store ephemeral usage events in existing usage pipeline (consistent format) to allow cost and behavior analysis.
FR-8: Provide an audit endpoint listing recent ephemeral events for a tenant (last 30 days).
telemetry_and_observability: Emit metrics: ephemeral_buffer_fill_ratio, ephemeral_spillover_count_per_tenant, ephemeral_tokens_consumed_total, ephemeral_denials_total.
SLO dashboards: per-pool and per-tenant 95/99/99.9 tail latency showing before/during/after ephemeral events.
Logging: structured events for every ephemeral admission/denial with tenant_id, pool_id, request_id, credits_before, credits_after, and decision_reason.
Alerts: high ephemeral_denials_total (>5% of pool requests over 5m) and more than 10 tenants simultaneously in negative-priority state.
Storage: keep raw ephemeral events in the existing telemetry retention window (30d) and aggregate for 90d for trend analysis.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature off by default; enable for internal dogfood reservations and run for 2 weeks. Verify telemetry and enforcement logic.
Phase 1 (opt-in): enable in Console as 'Ephemeral bridging' toggle for a small set of low-risk customers (10 customers). Monitor impact for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (graduated defaults): enable default behavior for new reservations with conservative caps; allow existing customers to opt-in via Console/API.
Phase 3 (guardrail enforcement): enable stricter denial messaging and add docs and playbook for Support and Sales; consider default enable for self-serve customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Simulated burst tests show ephemeral buffer reduces 429s by >=70% for spikes lasting <60s while not increasing 99th percentile latency for high-tier tenants by more than 2ms in controlled tests.
AC-2: Priority credit ledger records every ephemeral admission event and reconciles with usage pipeline within 1 minute of ingestion.
AC-3: Console shows the new toggles and per-reservation settings; changes propagate to runtime within 30s.
AC-4: Audit endpoint returns recent ephemeral events for a tenant and includes required fields in structured logs.
AC-5: Feature passes security review (KMS/RBAC considerations validated) and has no elevated attack surface in our threat model.
success_metrics: SM-1: Reduction in customer-observed 429s during short bursts by 40% across opt-in customers in first month.
SM-2: No more than 1.5x increase in provisioning churn or complaints from high-tier customers in first 30d post-rollout for opt-in customers.
SM-3: Telemetry shows average ephemeral_tokens_consumed_total per opt-in tenant < 5% of monthly committed tokens (controls spammy use).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: A single tenant could repeatedly burst and accumulate credits that crowd out others. Mitigation: implement per-tenant daily caps and decaying credit weight in scheduler.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: sample at pool-level for high-volume pools and provide aggregated metrics by default.
Risk: Unexpected billing disputes. Mitigation: clearly document that ephemeral bridging is not a billing credit; billing team to treat usage as normal until explicit pricing change is approved.
Risk: Complexity for operators. Mitigation: provide a concise on-call runbook and automated rollback toggle.
